## Data Acquisition and Introduction


For this project, we were given three different data sets that would help us evaluate the environmental efficiency of transit agencies in the United States.

1. **Energy Information Administration (EIA) State Electricity Profiles (`EIA_SEP_REPORT`)**:Examines the level of electrical grid carbon, the retail prices for electricity, and the total capacity generation. 
2. **National Transit Database (NTD) 2025 Energy Consumption (`NTD_ENERGY`)**:Takes a look at the annual fuel as well as the total electrical energy used across various modes when reporting the transit agency of the United States. 
3. **National Transit Database (NTD) 2025 Service Provided (`NTD_SERVICE`)**: Shows the annual ridership using passenger trips, total passenger miles, and demographics for the service area. 

### EIA State Electricity Profiles

```{r acquire-eia}
get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
  state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
  
  dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
  
  fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse = TRUE)
  
  if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
    BASE_URL <- "[https://www.eia.gov](https://www.eia.gov)"
    RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
      req_url_path("electricity", "state", state_formatted) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
      ) |>   
      req_retry(max_tries = 4) |>
      req_perform(file_name)
    
    resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
  }
  
  TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
    html_element("table") |> 
    html_table() |>
    mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
  
  if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
    TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
  }
  
  CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
    filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
    pull(Value) |> 
    str_replace_all(",", "") |>
    as.numeric()
  
  PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
    filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
    pull(Rank)
  
  RATE <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    as.numeric()
  
  GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    str_replace_all(",", "") |>
    as.numeric()
  
  data.frame(
    CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
    primary_source        = PRIMARY,
    electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, 
    generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
    state                 = state, 
    abbreviation          = abbr
  )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()
```

### NTD Energy Consumption

```{r acquire-ntd-energy}
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse = TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    request("[https://www.transit.dot.gov/](https://www.transit.dot.gov/)") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
    cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
    stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
  }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()
```

### NTD Transit Service Provided

```{r acquire-ntd-service}
load_ntd_service <- function(){
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse = TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    request("[https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv](https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv)") |>
      req_url_query(`$query` = paste(
        "SELECT `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`",
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000",
        sep = ",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |>
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }

  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
    cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
    stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.csv')` and try again.")
  }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```

## Data Cleaning and Preparation

> Prior to joining the NTD_Energy and NTD_Service data sets we have to recode the two letter name codes like "HR" (heavy rail) and "MB" (motorbus). We do this so it's easier for an individual to understand the context of the data through the tables and visuals provided below. In addition, NTD_ID helps prevent any potential mismatches and wrong joins in the table integration. The clearer the data the better. 


```{r recode-modes}
# Task 2: Recode two-letter Mode codes into descriptive names across both NTD tables
NTD_ENERGY <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(
    `NTD ID` = as.numeric(`NTD ID`),
    Mode = recode_values(Mode,
      "AR" ~ "Alaska Railroad",
      "CB" ~ "Commuter Bus",
      "CC" ~ "Cable Car",
      "CR" ~ "Commuter Rail",
      "DR" ~ "Demand Response",
      "FB" ~ "Ferryboat",
      "HR" ~ "Heavy Rail",
      "IP" ~ "Inclined Plane",
      "JT" ~ "Jitney",
      "LR" ~ "Light Rail",
      "MB" ~ "Motorbus",
      "MG" ~ "Monorail/Automated Guideway",
      "PB" ~ "Publico",
      "RB" ~ "Bus Rapid Transit",
      "SR" ~ "Streetcar Rail",
      "TB" ~ "Trolleybus",
      "TR" ~ "Aerial Tramway",
      "VP" ~ "Vanpool",
      "YR" ~ "Hybrid Rail",
      default = "Other/Unknown"
    )
  )

NTD_SERVICE <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID = as.numeric(NTD_ID),
    mode = recode_values(mode,
      "AR" ~ "Alaska Railroad",
      "CB" ~ "Commuter Bus",
      "CC" ~ "Cable Car",
      "CR" ~ "Commuter Rail",
      "DR" ~ "Demand Response",
      "FB" ~ "Ferryboat",
      "HR" ~ "Heavy Rail",
      "IP" ~ "Inclined Plane",
      "JT" ~ "Jitney",
      "LR" ~ "Light Rail",
      "MB" ~ "Motorbus",
      "MG" ~ "Monorail/Automated Guideway",
      "PB" ~ "Publico",
      "RB" ~ "Bus Rapid Transit",
      "SR" ~ "Streetcar Rail",
      "TB" ~ "Trolleybus",
      "TR" ~ "Aerial Tramway",
      "VP" ~ "Vanpool",
      "YR" ~ "Hybrid Rail",
      default = "Other/Unknown"
    )
  )
```

## Data Integration and Initial Exploration (8 Selected Questions)

### Task 3a: EIA State Electricity Profiles (Questions 1–4 of 8)

```{r eda-q1-q4-eia}
# --- Question 1 of 8 (Graph #1 - Task 3a Q1): 5 States with Most Expensive Electricity ---
plot_q1_expensive <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  slice_max(order_by = electricity_price_MWh, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(state, electricity_price_MWh), y = electricity_price_MWh, fill = primary_source)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = dollar(electricity_price_MWh, accuracy = 0.1)), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold") +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0, max(EIA_SEP_REPORT$electricity_price_MWh, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.15)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "Question 1 (Task 3a Q1): Top 5 States with the Most Expensive Retail Electricity",
    subtitle = "Average Retail Electricity Price ($ per MWh) by Primary Energy Source",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Average Retail Price ($ / MWh)",
    fill = "Primary Energy Source",
    caption = "Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) State Electricity Profiles"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "bottom")

# --- Question 2 of 8 (Table #1 - Task 3a Q2): 5 States with the 'Dirtiest' Electricity Mix ---
tbl_q2_dirtiest <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  slice_max(order_by = CO2_MWh, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  select(state, abbreviation, primary_source, CO2_MWh, electricity_price_MWh, generation_MWh) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Question 2 (Task 3a Q2): Top 5 States with the 'Dirtiest' Electricity Mix",
    subtitle = "Ranked by Highest Carbon Dioxide Emissions (lbs CO2 per MWh)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(CO2_MWh, generation_MWh), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_currency(columns = electricity_price_MWh, currency = "USD", decimals = 2) |>
  cols_label(
    state = "State",
    abbreviation = "Abbr",
    primary_source = "Primary Source",
    CO2_MWh = "CO2 Emissions (lbs/MWh)",
    electricity_price_MWh = "Retail Price ($/MWh)",
    generation_MWh = "Net Generation (MWh)"
  ) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13), heading.title.font.weight = "bold")

# --- Question 3 of 8 (Inline #1 - Task 3a Q3): US Weighted Average CO2 per MWh ---
us_weighted_co2_mwh <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  summarize(weighted_co2 = sum(CO2_MWh * generation_MWh, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(generation_MWh, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(weighted_co2)

# --- Question 4 of 8 (Inline #2 - Task 3a Q5): How many times cleaner is NY than Texas? ---
ny_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "NY") |> pull(CO2_MWh)
tx_co2 <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "TX") |> pull(CO2_MWh)
ny_vs_tx_ratio <- tx_co2 / ny_co2
```

```{r display-q1-q2, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
plot_q1_expensive
tbl_q2_dirtiest
```

* **Question 3 of 8 (Task 3a Q3 — Inline):** Using a generation-weighted average across all 50 states, the United States emits **`r comma(round(us_weighted_co2_mwh, 1))` lbs of $\text{CO}_2$ per MWh** of electricity produced.
* **Question 4 of 8 (Task 3a Q5 - Inline):** New York's electrical grid emits **`r comma(ny_co2)` lbs $\text{CO}_2\text{/MWh}$** compared to **`r comma(tx_co2)` lbs $\text{CO}_2\text{/MWh}$** in Texas, meaning New York's energy mix is **`r round(ny_vs_tx_ratio, 2)` times cleaner** than Texas's energy mix.

> 1. Looking at the data above, we can see that Hawaii has the most expensive retail electricity in the United States at $380. The reason why it is $109.6 more expensive than California is due to its geographical location (Pacific Ocean), meaning that it is not connected to mainland US and therefore lacks powergrid connections or pipelines unlike the other 49 states. Unlike the other four states, it relies on petroleum.

> 2. For this table, we can see that coal is considered the "dirtiest" primary energy source, and states like Kentucky, West Virginia, Wyoming, and Missouri all use it. The second is petroleum which is used by Hawaii as we discussed earlier. Once again, geography is the key factor behind states' decisions to use coal and petroleum. The first 4 states on the table are located near large coal reserves, making it easier for them to local sourced energy. same for Hawaii, geographical location makes it more difficult to find other sources of energy. As we can see, the difference in costs of energy between Hawaii and the other four states are striking. Because coal is locally sourced, the four states have lower prices (e.g.$91.40/MWh in Wyoming,$110.60/MWh in Missouri). In Hawaii, the price goes up to $380.00/MWh which shows how expensive liquid fuel can get.

> 3. This inline question tackles the weighted generation of energy across all states, but doesn't measure them all the same. For example, big energy generators like Texas aren't treated the same as smaller states like Vermont. Therefore, finding the average required as the baseline for the United States is quite important. The nation's average sits at 785 lbs CO2/MWh.

> 4. This inline question takes a look at the electrical grid emission of New York (537 lbs CO2/MWh) and Texas (823 lbs CO2/MWh). The reason why New York's energy is about 1.53 times cleaner than Texas is because the state utilizes more clean energy, whereas Texas heavily relies on its abundance of fossil fuels. Overall, Texas carbon intensity is way above the national average.

### Task 3b: NTD Energy Usage (Questions 5–6 of 8)

```{r eda-q5-q6-energy}
# --- Question 5 of 8 (Table #2 - Task 3b Q1): Top 5 Agencies by Total Fuel Gallons & Breakdown ---
tbl_q5_top_fuel <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(
    Diesel = sum(`Gallons of Diesel Fuel`, na.rm = TRUE),
    Gasoline = sum(`Gallons of Gasoline`, na.rm = TRUE),
    CNG = sum(`Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`, na.rm = TRUE),
    BioDiesel = sum(`Gallons of Bio-Diesel`, na.rm = TRUE),
    Other_Gallons = sum(
      `Gallons of Bunker Fuel` + `Gallons of Ethanol` + `Gallons of Kerosene` +
      `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas` + `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Total_Gallons = Diesel + Gasoline + CNG + BioDiesel + Other_Gallons,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  slice_max(order_by = Total_Gallons, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Question 5 (Task 3b Q1): Top 5 U.S. Transit Agencies by Total Gallons of Fuel Used",
    subtitle = "Breakdown by fuel type across all transit modes (2025 NTD Energy Data)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(Diesel, Gasoline, CNG, BioDiesel, Other_Gallons, Total_Gallons), decimals = 0) |>
  cols_label(
    `NTD ID` = "NTD ID",
    `Agency Name` = "Transit Agency",
    Diesel = "Diesel (Gal)",
    Gasoline = "Gasoline (Gal)",
    CNG = "CNG (Gal)",
    BioDiesel = "Bio-Diesel (Gal)",
    Other_Gallons = "Other Fuels (Gal)",
    Total_Gallons = "Total Fuel (Gal)"
  ) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13), heading.title.font.weight = "bold")

# --- Question 6 of 8 (Inline #3 - Task 3b Q3): Least commonly used fuel source ---
national_fuel_totals <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  select(
    `Gallons of Diesel Fuel`,
    `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`,
    `Gallons of Gasoline`,
    `Gallons of Bio-Diesel`,
    `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`,
    `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`,
    `Gallons of Bunker Fuel`,
    `Gallons of Ethanol`,
    `Gallons of Kerosene`
  ) |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Fuel_Type", values_to = "Total_Gallons") |>
  mutate(Fuel_Type = str_remove(Fuel_Type, "^Gallons of ")) |>
  arrange(Total_Gallons)

least_common_fuel <- national_fuel_totals |> slice_head(n = 1)
```

```{r display-q5}
tbl_q5_top_fuel
```

* **Question 6 of 8 (Task 3b Q3 — Inline):** Across all US public transit agencies, the least commonly used combustion fuel source is **`r least_common_fuel$Fuel_Type`**, with only **`r comma(least_common_fuel$Total_Gallons)` gallons** consumed nationwide.

> 5. This question takes a look at the transit agencies that use the most total gallons of fuel in the United States. New Jersey Transit Corporation sits at the very top with 41,721,414 gallons followed by MTA New York Transit at 40,816,461 total gallons for 2025. The primary source of fuel by four out of the five agencies shown is diesel, only the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority mostly uses CNG as its primary source. Four out of the five agencies shown are located in the Northeast, which makes sense due to its industrialization and largely populated cities. 

> 6. This question takes a look at the least commonly used source of fuel throughout the nation. The code shows that from all the types of fuel found in the data set provided, bunker fuel is the least commonly used with 0 gallons consumed across the United States. The truth is, bunker fuel is avoided by public transit agencies due to environmental regulations. Bunker fuel is mostly used by large cargo ships and tankers that carry various goods worldwide. It's not the safest source of energy to use in large municipalities.

### Task 3c: NTD Service Data (Questions 7–8 of 8)

```{r eda-q7-q8-service}
ntd_service_valid <- NTD_SERVICE |> filter(!flagged_likely_inaccurate)

# --- Question 7 of 8 (Graph #2 - Task 3c Q1): Top 5 Transit Services by Annual UPT ---
plot_q7_top_upt <- ntd_service_valid |>
  group_by(AGENCY, mode) |>
  summarize(Total_UPT = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(order_by = Total_UPT, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(Service_Label = str_wrap(paste0(AGENCY, " (", mode, ")"), width = 35)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Service_Label, Total_UPT), y = Total_UPT, fill = mode)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "Question 7 (Task 3c Q1): Top 5 U.S. Transit Services by Annual Ridership",
    subtitle = "Unlinked Passenger Trips (UPT) by Agency and Transit Mode",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Annual Unlinked Passenger Trips (UPT)",
    fill = "Transit Mode",
    caption = "Source: 2025 National Transit Database (NTD) Service Data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

# --- Question 8 of 8 (Inline #4 - Task 3c Q3): Average trip length on MTA NYC ---
mta_nyc_avg_trip <- ntd_service_valid |>
  filter(AGENCY == "MTA New York City Transit") |>
  summarize(avg_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(avg_miles)
```

## Multi-Table Data Analysis: Calculating Transit Emissions & The GTA Value Index

To compute the **Green Transit Alliance Value Index (GTA VI)**, we join `NTD_SERVICE`, `NTD_ENERGY`, and `EIA_SEP_REPORT` across agency, mode, and state keys. We then calculate:

1. **Direct Tailpipe Emissions ($\text{lbs CO}_2$)**: Applying standard EPA/EIA combustion emission factors to each liquid and gaseous fuel reported in `NTD_ENERGY`:
   * **Diesel Fuel**: $22.45\text{ lbs CO}_2/\text{gal}$
   * **Gasoline**: $19.60\text{ lbs CO}_2/\text{gal}$
   * **Bio-Diesel**: $21.00\text{ lbs CO}_2/\text{gal}$
   * **Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)**: $13.80\text{ lbs CO}_2/\text{gal (GGE)}$
   * **Liquified Natural Gas (LNG)**: $11.20\text{ lbs CO}_2/\text{gal}$
   * **Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG)**: $12.68\text{ lbs CO}_2/\text{gal}$
   * **Kerosene / Bunker Fuel**: $21.50\text{ lbs CO}_2/\text{gal}$
   * **Ethanol**: $12.70\text{ lbs CO}_2/\text{gal}$
2. **Upstream Electrical Grid Emissions ($\text{lbs CO}_2$)**: Converting agency electrical consumption (`Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion` + `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`) from $\text{kWh}$ to $\text{MWh}$ ($\div 1,000$) and multiplying by the agency state's `CO2_MWh` emission factor from `EIA_SEP_REPORT`.
3. **Counterfactual Driving Emissions & GTA Value Index (GTA VI)**:
   * Using the EPA average passenger vehicle fuel economy ($25.4\text{ MPG}$ at $19.60\text{ lbs CO}_2/\text{gal} \approx 0.7717\text{ lbs CO}_2\text{ per passenger-mile}$), we estimate the counterfactual tailpipe emissions if every transit rider had instead driven their trip.
   * **Net $\text{CO}_2$ Saved ($\text{lbs}$)** $= \text{Counterfactual Driving Emissions} - \text{Total Transit Emissions}$.
   * **Emissions Saved per Passenger Mile ($\text{lbs CO}_2/\text{mile}$)** $= \frac{\text{Net CO}_2\text{ Saved}}{\text{Total Passenger Miles}}$, which serves as our normalized efficiency score across **Small**, **Medium**, and **Large** transit agencies.

> In order to get into more depth with data analysis, we have to join all data sets provided (NTD_SERVICE, NTD_ ENERGY, EIA_SEP_REPORT). By doing this, we are able to identify nationwide agencies from small to large, see the various transit modes, as well as the location of the agencies. When looking at the data, it's important to include each state's electrical grid carbon intensity due to the fact that electric transit vehicles as well hybrid have a carbon footprint which is connected locally. This way it's easier to reward cleaner fuel sources and penalizing agencies that use "dirty" sources like coal and petroleum which negatively impact our environment. Lastly, to avoid big agencies like NYC MTA Transit skewing our data due to their size, we split the agencies into small, medium, and large levels which allows for a fair analysis.

```{r join-multi-table}
# Step 1: Aggregate NTD_SERVICE by (NTD_ID, AGENCY, city, state, mode)
service_by_mode <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  filter(!flagged_likely_inaccurate) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, AGENCY, city, state, mode) |>
  summarize(
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    sum_passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(total_upt > 0, sum_passenger_miles > 0)

# Step 2: Create a state lookup from EIA_SEP_REPORT matching both abbreviation and full state name
eia_lookup <- bind_rows(
  EIA_SEP_REPORT |> mutate(state_key = str_to_upper(str_trim(abbreviation))),
  EIA_SEP_REPORT |> mutate(state_key = str_to_upper(str_trim(state)))
) |>
  distinct(state_key, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(state_key, CO2_MWh, primary_source, electricity_price_MWh)

# Fallback national average for territories/DC if not in 50-state table
nat_avg_co2 <- mean(EIA_SEP_REPORT$CO2_MWh, na.rm = TRUE)
nat_avg_price <- mean(EIA_SEP_REPORT$electricity_price_MWh, na.rm = TRUE)

# Step 3: Join NTD_SERVICE with NTD_ENERGY and EIA_SEP_REPORT
transit_emissions_mode <- service_by_mode |>
  inner_join(
    NTD_ENERGY,
    by = c("NTD_ID" = "NTD ID", "mode" = "Mode")
  ) |>
  mutate(state_key = str_to_upper(str_trim(state))) |>
  left_join(eia_lookup, by = "state_key") |>
  mutate(
    CO2_MWh = replace_na(CO2_MWh, nat_avg_co2),
    electricity_price_MWh = replace_na(electricity_price_MWh, nat_avg_price),
    primary_source = replace_na(primary_source, "Natural Gas"),
    
    # Calculate Direct Tailpipe Fuel Emissions (lbs CO2)
    direct_fuel_co2_lbs =
      `Gallons of Diesel Fuel` * 22.45 +
      `Gallons of Gasoline` * 19.60 +
      `Gallons of Bio-Diesel` * 21.00 +
      `Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas` * 13.80 +
      `Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas` * 11.20 +
      `Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas` * 12.68 +
      `Gallons of Bunker Fuel` * 24.70 +
      `Gallons of Kerosene` * 21.50 +
      `Gallons of Ethanol` * 12.70,
    
    # Calculate Upstream Electric Grid Emissions (lbs CO2)
    total_electric_kwh = `Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion` + `Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`,
    upstream_electric_co2_lbs = (total_electric_kwh / 1000) * CO2_MWh,
    
    # Total Transit Emissions (lbs CO2)
    total_co2_lbs = direct_fuel_co2_lbs + upstream_electric_co2_lbs,
    
    # Emissions Efficiency Metrics
    co2_per_upt_lbs = total_co2_lbs / total_upt,
    co2_per_pass_mile_lbs = total_co2_lbs / sum_passenger_miles
  )

# Display interactive mode-level emissions table
transit_emissions_mode |>
  arrange(co2_per_pass_mile_lbs) |>
  select(
    AGENCY, city, state, mode, total_upt, sum_passenger_miles,
    direct_fuel_co2_lbs, upstream_electric_co2_lbs, total_co2_lbs, co2_per_pass_mile_lbs
  ) |>
  head(100) |>
  DT::datatable(
    colnames = c(
      "Agency", "City", "State", "Mode", "Trips (UPT)", "Passenger Miles",
      "Fuel CO2 (lbs)", "Electric CO2 (lbs)", "Total CO2 (lbs)", "CO2 / Pass Mile (lbs)"
    ),
    options = list(pageLength = 8, scrollX = TRUE),
    caption = "Table 5: Mode-Level Transit Emissions and Efficiency (Top 100 Most Efficient Agency-Modes)"
  ) |>
  formatRound(
    columns = c("total_upt", "sum_passenger_miles", "direct_fuel_co2_lbs", "upstream_electric_co2_lbs", "total_co2_lbs"),
    digits = 0
  ) |>
  formatRound(columns = "co2_per_pass_mile_lbs", digits = 3)
```

```{r calculate-gta-vi}
# Aggregate to the Agency level and classify into Small, Medium, and Large tiers
CAR_CO2_PER_MILE_LBS <- 19.60 / 25.4 # ~0.7717 lbs CO2 per mile for average US passenger vehicle

agency_gta_scores <- transit_emissions_mode |>
  group_by(NTD_ID, AGENCY, city, state, primary_source, CO2_MWh) |>
  summarize(
    Total_UPT = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Passenger_Miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    Direct_Fuel_CO2_Lbs = sum(direct_fuel_co2_lbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    Electric_CO2_Lbs = sum(upstream_electric_co2_lbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Transit_CO2_Lbs = sum(total_co2_lbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Electric_kWh = sum(total_electric_kwh, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # Require meaningful commercial transit scale (at least 100,000 annual trips)
  filter(Total_UPT >= 100000, Total_Passenger_Miles >= 100000, Total_Transit_CO2_Lbs > 0) |>
  # Categorize into Small, Medium, and Large agencies based on tertiles of Total UPT
  mutate(
    Size_Category = case_when(
      Total_UPT >= quantile(Total_UPT, 2/3, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Large Agency",
      Total_UPT >= quantile(Total_UPT, 1/3, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Medium Agency",
      TRUE ~ "Small Agency"
    ),
    Size_Category = factor(Size_Category, levels = c("Large Agency", "Medium Agency", "Small Agency")),
    
    # Per-unit emissions
    CO2_per_UPT_Lbs = Total_Transit_CO2_Lbs / Total_UPT,
    CO2_per_Mile_Lbs = Total_Transit_CO2_Lbs / Total_Passenger_Miles,
    
    # Counterfactual Passenger Car Emissions & Net Emissions Avoided
    Counterfactual_Car_CO2_Lbs = Total_Passenger_Miles * CAR_CO2_PER_MILE_LBS,
    Net_CO2_Saved_Tons = (Counterfactual_Car_CO2_Lbs - Total_Transit_CO2_Lbs) / 2000,
    
    # GTA Value Index (GTA VI): lbs CO2 avoided per passenger mile relative to driving
    GTA_VI_Score = CAR_CO2_PER_MILE_Lbs <- (CAR_CO2_PER_MILE_LBS - CO2_per_Mile_Lbs)
  )
```

## Deliverable: Green Transit Alliance (GTA VI) Annual Press Release

> The Green Transit Alliance (GTA) presents to you its annual press release. For this year, we present the annual award winners & finalists across small, medium, and large transit agencies, the Electrification & Clean Grid Award, as well as some concerns that should be addressed to help our environment. 
>
>  The champion across the nation's large agencies is the Anaheim Transportation Network, which managed to save a total of 0.679 lbs CO2/mile. The battle for the first spot was very narrow and could have gone either way, but unfortunately for the Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon, it lost by 0.006 lbs CO2/mile (total 0.673 saved). At the third spot we have the California Vanpool Authority with 0.626 lbs CO2/mile saved. Despite the fact that it fell short in saved lbs CO2/mile, the Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon saved over 90,000 tons of net CO2 which is remarkable considering its annual 65,659,766 trips. Moving on to the champion awards for medium agencies, we present to you the City of Seattle, dba: Seattle Center Monorail. The total of 0.708 lbs CO2/mile doesn't just make it the champion of medium agencies, but the champion of all agencies! Congratulations. In second place we have Metropolitan Transportation Commission, dba: MTC with 0.609 lbs CO2/mile saved and in third San Diego Association of Governments, dba: SANDAG with 0.602 lbs CO2/mile saved. Although they couldn't get close to reaching City of Seattle, dba: Seattle Center Monorail's GTA VI (lbs Saved/Mi), their saved net CO2 cannot be overlooked with 18,824 and 14,391 tons respectively. Lastly, we have the champion of small agencies. First place goes to Adirondack Transit Lines, Inc., dba: Adirondack Trailways with 0.626 lbs CO2/miles saved. Second place goes to Hampton Jitney, Inc. with 0.603 lbs CO2/miles saved, and at third place we have Denver Regional Council of Governments with a total 0.600 lbs CO2/mile saved. Hampton Jitney, Inc.'s  17,955 tons of net CO2 saved is noteworthy to mention considering its smaller size. I would like to congratulate all 9 agencies that were a part of our awards, especially the west coast for having 6 agencies make up the list!
>  
>  Now, we present to you the Electrification & Clean Grid Award. For this award, we take a look at the agencies which were capable of converging low carbon regional power grids to get very low (close to zero) life cycle emissions. It's always remarkable to operate below the average benchmark 0.77 lbs CO2 per passenger-mile, and the finalists of the award all managed to do it. These agencies are all powered by clean energy grids and help our cause of setting healthier environmental standards. With that being said, the top agency City of Seattle, dba: Seattle Center Monorail managed to get 0.064 lbs Transit CO2/Mi. For the second and third place we have the Anaheim Transportation Network, dba: Anaheim Regional Transportation at 0.093 lbs Transit CO2/Mi and Tri-County Metropolitan Transportation District of Oregon, dba: TriMet at 0.099lbs Transit CO2/Mi. Their efforts help suppress emissions per passenger below the 0.10lb mark, showing that electrically powered vehicles and clean energy as a whole can help the environment.  
>  
> Before signing off, I would like to address the elephant in the room which the data we gathered showed. By addressing this issue we can make improvements that will help our cause. The truth is that the nationwide majority of small and medium agencies do not provide any benefits in regards to carbon. It's fascinating how some of these agencies generate 1.5 to 3 lbs CO2/mi, which means that pollution levels are doubled or quadrupled compared to the rates generated by an individual driving an automobile for example. One of the main reasons behind this underperformance is the presence of routes with low densities which in addition have low ridership. Large agencies utilize fuel much more efficiently and have bigger riderships as well as higher density routes. This results in them reaching 100 million passenger miles while comfortably staying below the nationwide benchmark of 0.77 lbs CO2/mi. We can tackle these issues by having small and medium agencies purchase smaller vehicles which will meet their ridership needs and result in net CO2 savings. 
>  
>  As we take the time to celebrate our achievements and analyze the improvements we can make to protect the environment, we should always remind all individuals how important clean energy is. We have to make our voices heard and our message clear, the United States of America is more than capable of building a clean energy transit system to help protect our environment. 
>  
>  Sincerely, 
>
> **Konstantinos Gkanas** 
>
>  Executive Director of Green Transit Alliance (GTA)
  
  
  
  
  
  
```{r tbl-gta-winners}
# Identify the Top 3 GTA VI Award Finalists in each Size Category (Large, Medium, Small)
gta_winners <- agency_gta_scores |>
  group_by(Size_Category) |>
  slice_max(order_by = GTA_VI_Score, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(Award_Rank = paste0("#", row_number())) |>
  ungroup()

gta_winners |>
  select(
    Size_Category, Award_Rank, AGENCY, city, state,
    Total_UPT, Total_Passenger_Miles, CO2_per_UPT_Lbs, CO2_per_Mile_Lbs, GTA_VI_Score, Net_CO2_Saved_Tons
  ) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Size_Category") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Table 6: Green Transit Alliance (GTA VI) Annual Award Winners & Finalists",
    subtitle = "Top 3 Greenest Public Transit Agencies by Size Category (Normalized per UPT & per Passenger Mile)"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(Total_UPT, Total_Passenger_Miles, Net_CO2_Saved_Tons), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(CO2_per_UPT_Lbs, CO2_per_Mile_Lbs, GTA_VI_Score), decimals = 3) |>
  cols_label(
    Award_Rank = "Rank",
    AGENCY = "Transit Agency",
    city = "City",
    state = "State",
    Total_UPT = "Annual Trips (UPT)",
    Total_Passenger_Miles = "Passenger Miles",
    CO2_per_UPT_Lbs = "Transit CO2/UPT (lbs)",
    CO2_per_Mile_Lbs = "Transit CO2/Mi (lbs)",
    GTA_VI_Score = "GTA VI (lbs Saved/Mi)",
    Net_CO2_Saved_Tons = "Net CO2 Saved (Tons)"
  ) |>
  data_color(
    columns = GTA_VI_Score,
    palette = "Greens"
  ) |>
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = px(13),
    heading.title.font.weight = "bold",
    row_group.font.weight = "bold"
  )
```

```{r tbl-least-efficient}
# Highlight the Top 5 Total Volume Savers vs. 5 Agencies Needing Electrification/Load Factor Improvements
bind_rows(
  agency_gta_scores |>
    slice_max(order_by = Net_CO2_Saved_Tons, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(Award_Group = "Heavyweight Climate Champions (Highest Total Tons CO2 Avoided)"),
  agency_gta_scores |>
    slice_min(order_by = GTA_VI_Score, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(Award_Group = "Diesel & Low-Occupancy Watchlist (Lowest GTA VI Efficiency)")
) |>
  select(
    Award_Group, AGENCY, city, state, Size_Category,
    Total_Passenger_Miles, CO2_per_Mile_Lbs, GTA_VI_Score, Net_CO2_Saved_Tons
  ) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Award_Group") |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Table 7: Total Volume Climate Champions vs. Low-Efficiency Watchlist",
    subtitle = "Comparing absolute national carbon reduction leaders against low-occupancy systems"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(Total_Passenger_Miles, Net_CO2_Saved_Tons), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(CO2_per_Mile_Lbs, GTA_VI_Score), decimals = 3) |>
  cols_label(
    AGENCY = "Transit Agency",
    city = "City",
    state = "State",
    Size_Category = "Tier",
    Total_Passenger_Miles = "Passenger Miles",
    CO2_per_Mile_Lbs = "Transit CO2/Mi (lbs)",
    GTA_VI_Score = "GTA VI Score",
    Net_CO2_Saved_Tons = "Net CO2 Saved (Tons)"
  ) |>
```

```{r plot-gta-winners, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
# Bar chart of the Top 5 Agencies per Size Category by Emissions per Passenger Mile vs. Passenger Car Benchmark
agency_gta_scores |>
  group_by(Size_Category) |>
  slice_max(order_by = GTA_VI_Score, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(Agency_Wrapped = str_wrap(AGENCY, width = 38)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Agency_Wrapped, -CO2_per_Mile_Lbs), y = CO2_per_Mile_Lbs, fill = Size_Category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = CAR_CO2_PER_MILE_LBS, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0, 0.85)) +
  facet_wrap(~Size_Category, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  labs(
    title = "Figure 2: GTA VI Award Finalists — Carbon Emissions per Passenger Mile",
    subtitle = "Top 5 Large, Medium, and Small Systems vs. U.S. Car Benchmark (Red Dashed Line = 0.77 lbs CO2/mi)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Carbon Emissions (lbs CO2 per Passenger Mile)",
    fill = "Agency Tier",
    caption = "Sources: 2025 National Transit Database (NTD) & EIA State Electricity Profiles"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
```

